text:
mira: quick heads-up — ran a multi-GPU attention kernel sweep (A100 / H100 / L40S) across seq lengths 64/128/256/512/1024/2048/4096 and batch sizes 1/2/4/8/16. focusing on: kernel selection boundaries, slot-based batching heuristics, and KV-cache prefetch/eviction behavior. dashboard: https://perf.internal/r/1977501234 :eyes:

devin: nice. any obvious regressions or tail spikes?

mira: median p99 pipeline looks stable except H100 at seq=512, b=8 where fused kernel shows a 25–30% 99.9th tail regression vs the spillaware kernel. hypothesis: prefetch-window misprediction causing KV cache thrash -> stalls. also saw a smaller L40S perf cliff at seq>=2048 when using continuous-batching enabled.

cheng: can you paste the raw numbers for H100 seq=512 b=8? want to see CPU-side enqueue latency too.

mira: pasted short excerpt (micro-benchmark, single model, 64 layer-ish):
```
H100 | seq=512 | b=8 | kernel=spillaware-fused-v2 | median=34.2ms | p99=89.1ms | p99.9=153.7ms | tokens/sec=420
H100 | seq=512 | b=8 | kernel=paired-async | median=36.0ms | p99=72.3ms  | p99.9=112.5ms | tokens/sec=410
A100 | seq=512 | b=8 | kernel=spillaware-fused-v2 | median=48.8ms | p99=120.2ms | p99.9=210.4ms | tokens/sec=280
L40S | seq=2048 | b=4 | kernel=continuous-batch | median=210ms  | p99=860ms   | p99.9=1.4s   | tokens/sec=95
```

olga: that gap between fused and paired-async on H100 p99.9 is worrying. sounds like KV eviction hammering under certain batch/seq shapes. did the run include KV-prefetch tuned flags?

mira: prefetch window set to default (pf_window=12 tokens). ablation toggles: pf_window=6 reduced p99.9 by ~40% but increased median slightly. disabling prefix caching (kv_cache=false) collapsed the regression but obviously not acceptable for production.

devin: could be a race where fused kernel expects contiguous KV layout and prefetch steps reorder evictions, causing a small burst of remote memory reads. Suggest two experiments: (1) add a light-weight backoff in kernel selection: if predicted tail>threshold swap to paired-async, (2) binary-search the batch-size threshold where selection flips (we need an automated runner).

cheng: agree. I'll prototype a heuristic: keep a per-(seq,model) rolling estimate of tail-latency and add a hysteresis window when switching kernels. pseudocode:
```
if tail_p99.9(current_profile) > tail_threshold and current_kernel == fused:
  candidate = spillaware
  if tail_p99.9(candidate) < tail_threshold * 0.9:
    switch_to(candidate)
else if median_improvement(candidate) > median_gain_threshold:
  prefer(candidate)
```

mira: that seems reasonable. also want to explore a "prefetch-padding" approach — extend pf_window by 2 tokens for a few warm requests to avoid eviction storms.

olga: can we get perf-bot to run a focused grid: H100 seq=[256,512,1024], batch=[4,8,16], pf_window=[6,12,16], kernel=[fused,spillaware,paired-async]? include enqueue and CPU-tail breakdowns.

perf-bot: queued job 1977501234-01. expected runtime ~2h. will post condensed CSV and flamegraphs to https://perf.internal/jobs/1977501234-01 once finished. cc @mira @cheng

devin: also note to add a small JVM/worker-side throttle: if enqueue_latency spikes > 50ms repeatedly, temporarily limit in-flight batches to mitigate KV pressure. helped in earlier kv-spill tests.

mira: thanks all. next steps: (1) perf-bot run above, (2) cheng protos hysteresis switching and simulated replay with captured traces, (3) olga runs KV eviction microbench to validate prefetch-padding. I'll open a short PR with logging hooks for kernel-selection decisions so we can correlate traces with model requests (should help root-cause). :memo:

olga: +1, will also add a regression alert for p99.9 jumps > 2x for any (seq,batch) bucket for H100.

perf-bot: job 1977501234-01 finished. artifacts: https://perf.internal/jobs/1977501234-01/artifacts.csv (summary attached), flamegraphs: https://perf.internal/jobs/1977501234-01/flame.html. short summary: prefetch_window=6 reduced p99.9 by 38% for fused on H100 seq=512 b=8 but reduced median tokens/sec by ~3%.

mira: perfect — will triage the artifacts and follow up with a small canary config change in staging to enable prefetch-padding + hysteresis kernel selection. any objections?

devin: none from me. thanks for running this so quickly. :rocket:
